model.name: No real iOS Safari test capability — acquire a real iOS Safari path (device or cloud service); Playwright WebKit (Linux) misses iOS-Safari-version-specific bugs
model.description: CAPABILITY GAP (tester-named, PO 2026-09-05; a real weakness, not a one-off): WE HAVE NO REAL iOS SAFARI TEST CAPABILITY. Playwright WebKit IS Linux WebKit and does NOT carry iOS-Safari-version-specific bugs — this exact service-worker STREAMED-BODY DROP was INVISIBLE to it. CONSEQUENCE (stated honestly): iOS-only defects will keep reaching us through TRON DEVICE rather than through our gates, and any iOS-specific AC we write can only ever be CODE-PROOF + SIGNATURE-MATCH, NEVER device-verified BY US. That is a GAP IN WHAT OUR GREENS CAN MEAN, so it belongs on the RECORD, not in someone memory. FRAME: acquire a real iOS Safari path (a physical device OR a cloud device service). This is WHY Tron keeps finding what we cannot.

discoverySource.workedExample: service-worker streamed-body drop, invisible to Playwright WebKit, reached us via Tron device
discoverySource.notSecurity: this is a device/browser TEST-CAPABILITY gap (iOS Safari), NOT the killed owner-auth harness — no auth/credential/owner.

An R40.88 instance: a ruling about what our iOS greens can mean, carrying a failable guard (no-false-iOS-device-verification-claim). Ties customer-not-tester (the harness gap IS the defect) + recurring-report-one-home (iOS defects route here).
